mutations.name: authentication dependency replaced by a constant subject
mutations.boundary: Every business route must require a verified bearer token; the identity chain must begin at get_current_user and nowhere else.

mutations.name: JWT verification bypassed: claims read without decoding
mutations.boundary: Claims may only be trusted after signature, expiry, issuer and audience verification against the published JWKS.

mutations.name: client-provided user_id claim overrides the resolved actor identity
mutations.boundary: Actor identity is the database user row selected by the verified `sub`; no other token field may name the actor.

mutations.name: client-provided organization_id claim overrides tenant authority
mutations.boundary: Tenant authority is derived server-side from the user row; a token claim must never select the organization.

mutations.name: students_select becomes globally permissive: USING (true)
mutations.boundary: A member of one organization must not SELECT another organization's student rows.

mutations.name: assessments_select becomes globally permissive: USING (true)
mutations.boundary: A member of one organization must not SELECT another organization's assessment rows.

mutations.name: intervention_plans_select becomes globally permissive: USING (true)
mutations.boundary: A member of one organization must not SELECT another organization's intervention plans.

mutations.name: assessment_results_select becomes globally permissive: USING (true)
mutations.boundary: A member of one organization must not SELECT another organization's assessment results.

mutations.name: aeos_has_org_access stops requiring an ACTIVE organization
mutations.boundary: Suspending an organization must immediately remove read access through RLS.

mutations.name: aeos_can_write_org stops requiring an ACTIVE organization
mutations.boundary: Suspending an organization must immediately remove write authority through RLS.

mutations.name: aeos_is_org_admin stops requiring an ACTIVE organization
mutations.boundary: Suspending an organization must immediately remove admin authority through RLS.

mutations.name: actor resolution stops requiring an ACTIVE organization
mutations.boundary: Suspending an organization must immediately remove access on the FastAPI request path, which uses the RLS-bypassing service role.

mutations.name: aeos_has_org_access stops requiring an ACTIVE membership
mutations.boundary: Deactivating a membership must immediately remove access through RLS.

mutations.name: actor resolution accepts inactive users
mutations.boundary: A disabled user must not resolve to an actor on the FastAPI request path.

mutations.name: students_delete widened from admin back to any teacher
mutations.boundary: DELETE of a student is reserved to organization admins.

mutations.name: students_insert drops the created_by actor binding
mutations.boundary: An inserted row must record the acting user; created_by may not name another user.

mutations.name: assessments_insert FK tenant check collapsed to a tautology
mutations.boundary: An assessment may only reference a student in the same organization.

mutations.name: ownership columns become mutable (identity trigger neutered)
mutations.boundary: organization_id and created_by may never be changed by an UPDATE.

mutations.name: list endpoint drops its tenant filter
mutations.boundary: Every service-role query must carry the server-derived organization_id; list endpoints must not return other tenants' rows.

mutations.name: get-by-id endpoint drops its tenant filter
mutations.boundary: Every service-role query must carry the server-derived organization_id; fetch-by-id must not expose another tenant's row.

mutations.name: browser falls back to the service-role key when no user token is present
mutations.boundary: The service-role credential bypasses RLS and must never be reachable from an ordinary (browser) request; only a user bearer token may authorize one.
mutations.precheck: textual substitution (no build step in this harness)

mutations.name: missing credentials fall through to a default authenticated subject
mutations.boundary: Absent or non-bearer credentials must fail closed with 401, never resolve to a default identity.

mutations.name: role authorization always allows
mutations.boundary: Role authorization must deny by default; an actor outside the allow list may not perform a privileged write.

mutations.name: expired tokens accepted (verify_exp disabled)
mutations.boundary: An expired token must be rejected.

mutations.name: wrong issuer accepted (verify_iss disabled)
mutations.boundary: A token issued by anyone other than the configured Supabase issuer must be rejected.

mutations.name: audience validation removed (wrong or absent audience accepted)
mutations.boundary: A token minted for another audience, or carrying no audience claim at all, must be rejected.

mutations.name: invalid signature accepted (verify_signature disabled)
mutations.boundary: A token not signed by a published Supabase key must be rejected.

mutations.name: symmetric (oct) published keys accepted as HS256
mutations.boundary: A shared secret must never verify a token, even one published in the JWKS; otherwise anyone who can read the JWKS can mint any session.

mutations.name: verification algorithm taken from the token header
mutations.boundary: The algorithm is pinned by the published key the `kid` selects; the token's own `alg` header may not choose it.

mutations.name: raw JWKS entry handed to python-jose instead of the checked key
mutations.boundary: The key that verifies the signature must be exactly the published entry whose type and curve were checked, not keys nested inside it.

mutations.name: missing key ID falls back to the first published key
mutations.boundary: A token whose header carries no `kid` must be rejected; the verification key may not be guessed.

mutations.name: unknown key ID falls back to the first published key
mutations.boundary: A token whose `kid` matches no published key must be rejected; otherwise key rotation and revocation are meaningless.

mutations.name: malformed tokens fall through to a default authenticated subject
mutations.boundary: Any JWT parse or validation error must fail closed with 401; the error path may not return an identity.

mutations.name: unusable published keys escape the 401 handler as server errors
mutations.boundary: Every JOSE error on the verification path, including a key the caller's kid selects but python-jose cannot use, must fail closed with 401.

mutations.name: tokens without an expiry claim accepted
mutations.boundary: A token must carry `exp`; python-jose treats the claim as optional, so without the explicit check a token minted without one never expires.

mutations.name: cached key set never expires, so revoked keys keep verifying
mutations.boundary: A key the issuer stops publishing must stop verifying within the cache's maximum age; a matching cached kid never forces a refresh.

mutations.name: failed refresh falls back to the expired key set
mutations.boundary: When a due key-set refresh fails, verification must fail closed rather than keep trusting keys whose freshness can no longer be shown.

mutations.name: every unknown key ID forces a key-set fetch
mutations.boundary: An invented `kid` is read before any signature check, so it may force at most one refresh per interval; otherwise anonymous requests drive unbounded traffic to the key endpoint and real users get 503.

mutations.name: client roles keep TRUNCATE on existing tables
mutations.boundary: TRUNCATE is not subject to row-level security, so a client role holding it can empty every tenant's rows regardless of policy.

mutations.name: tables created later regain TRUNCATE from the default privileges
mutations.boundary: Revoking TRUNCATE from today's tables is not enough; the standing default grant must not hand it to the next migration's tables.

mutations.name: default-privilege revoke issued globally instead of for schema public
mutations.boundary: A global default-privilege REVOKE does not take back a per-schema default GRANT, so tables created later in public regain TRUNCATE.

mutations.name: anon keeps TRUNCATE on existing tables
mutations.boundary: The unauthenticated client role must not hold a privilege RLS does not govern; revoking from `authenticated` alone leaves anon able to empty every tenant's rows.

mutations.name: client roles keep MAINTAIN on existing tables (PostgreSQL 17)
mutations.boundary: MAINTAIN is not subject to row-level security; a client role holding it can REINDEX or CLUSTER, and so exclusively lock and rewrite, every tenant's table.

mutations.name: tables created later regain MAINTAIN from the default privileges
mutations.boundary: Revoking MAINTAIN from today's tables is not enough; the standing default grant must not hand it to the next migration's tables.

mutations.name: ai_recommendations_delete widened to any authenticated user
mutations.boundary: A WHERE-less DELETE never consults the SELECT policy, so the DELETE policy's USING clause alone must stop another tenant, a suspended tenant or a disabled account from removing a tenant's rows.

mutations.name: service lets any organization member read any feedback draft
mutations.boundary: Inside one organization only the requesting teacher and org admins may read a draft and the student response it holds.

mutations.name: service lets an admin decide another teacher's draft
mutations.boundary: Only the teacher who requested a draft may accept, revise or reject it; an admin reads for oversight but does not decide for the teacher.

mutations.name: ownership read helper widened to any organization member
mutations.boundary: The database must not show a peer teacher or support staff another teacher's requests, drafts or decisions through the data API.

mutations.name: ai_feedback_requests_select reverted to the 006 org-wide policy
mutations.boundary: A request row holds the student's response; a peer teacher must not read it.

mutations.name: ai_feedback_drafts_select reverted to the 006 org-wide policy
mutations.boundary: A peer teacher must not read another teacher's AI draft.

mutations.name: ai_feedback_decisions_select reverted to the 006 org-wide policy
mutations.boundary: A peer teacher must not read another teacher's decisions.

mutations.name: decision trigger accepts any active teacher or admin as the decider
mutations.boundary: The database refuses a decision recorded by anyone other than the teacher who requested the draft, even from the service role.

mutations.name: anon keeps EXECUTE on the SECURITY DEFINER helpers
mutations.boundary: The helpers read membership with RLS bypassed; PostgREST serves them at /rest/v1/rpc/<name>, so the anon key alone must not run them.

mutations.name: helpers created later are executable by anon
mutations.boundary: Revoking EXECUTE from today's helpers is not enough; the standing default grant must not hand it to the next migration's helpers.
